answer: I'd like to talk about something I read every week without fail. A publication I genuinely enjoy reading is a weekly current-affairs magazine that covers global news and analysis. It's an English-language magazine that deals with politics, economics, science and culture from around the world, along with longer features and book reviews. I read it regularly, usually at the weekend when I have time to digest it properly. I normally go through it on my laptop on Friday mornings with a cup of tea, and then return to a couple of the longer articles on Saturday evening. What I appreciate most is the depth of its reporting; unlike quick news headlines, it offers thoughtful, [[in-depth]] analysis. It helps me understand the context behind major events, which I find genuinely [[enlightening]]. That is especially useful in my job, because students often ask me about the situation in the countries they hope to study in. The writing is intelligent without being pretentious, which makes even complex topics accessible. Reading it keeps me well [[informed]] about the world in a way that scrolling social media never could. Honestly, in an age of shallow, rapid news consumption, I value having a source that encourages proper reflection. It has also noticeably improved my vocabulary and general knowledge over time. I think it is important to consume some [[substantial]] content rather than just quick, fragmented updates. It has become a genuinely enjoyable weekend ritual that leaves me feeling both informed and [[intellectually stimulated]].

followUps.q: Do you ever read local newspapers too?
followUps.answer: Yes, I skim a Bengali daily newspaper most mornings over breakfast, mainly for national news. The magazine is for deeper reading, whereas the newspaper keeps me [[up to date]] with what's happening at home.

followUps.q: Do you prefer reading news in print or online?
followUps.answer: Online, mostly, because it's quicker and more convenient. That said, my father still insists on a printed newspaper every morning, and I do enjoy sharing it with him over tea.
